react_result.final_narrative_text: Four independent pathway-enrichment tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged DB) ranks KEGG:map00380 and WP:WP465 first with FDR = 3.4e-15 and fold-enrichment ≈ 750; six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde) overlap this pathway. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with raw p = 5.41e-09, hitting the identical six compounds plus a structural isomer of 4-hydroxyretinoic acid. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scores the same pathway first (p = 0.00202, overlap 13/14 compounds in the human_mfn network), and additionally flags Vitamin A (retinol) metabolism via 4-hydroxyretinoic acid. RaMP also flags the Reactome module REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis, FDR = 3.59e-08) and WikiPathways WP:WP550 (Biogenic amine synthesis, FDR = 3.98e-08). The molybdenum atom (C00150) did not enrich any pathway and the reconcile_inchikey check confirmed its user-supplied InChIKey (MMVYPOCJESWGTC) is a distinct connectivity cluster from the canonical CHEBI:28685 entry, indicating an elemental-cofactor artefact. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism spanning the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), the biogenic-amine branch (serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine), and the aldehyde intermediate (indoleacetaldehyde), with a secondary hit to retinoic acid hydroxylation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism first with FDR = 3.44e-15 and fold-enrichment of 750.6, driven by six input metabolites hitting the pathway including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with raw p = 5.41e-09, reporting six overlapping compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity on the human_mfn network ranks MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism first with p = 0.00286, overlapping 7 compounds from the 14-member reference set and providing orthogonal empirical-compound confirmation. Reactome module REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis appears at rank 3 in the RaMP results with FDR = 3.59e-08, and WikiPathways WP:WP550 Biogenic amine synthesis ranks 5th with FDR = 3.98e-08. The converging evidence across ORA, KEGG PSEA, and m/z-network paradigms identifies coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism as the primary biological story. The driver metabolites span both the biogenic-amine branch (L-tryptophan as substrate, serotonin and melatonin as products via tryptophan 5-monooxygenase, EC 1.13.11.11) and the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid as a downstream intermediate).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism first with FDR = 3.44e-15 and fold-enrichment of 750.6, driven by six input metabolites hitting the pathway including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with raw p = 5.41e-09, reporting six overlapping compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity on the human_mfn network ranks MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism first with p = 0.00286, overlapping 7 compounds from the 14-member reference set and providing orthogonal empirical-compound confirmation. Reactome module REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis appears at rank 3 in the RaMP results with FDR = 3.59e-08, and WikiPathways WP:WP550 Biogenic amine synthesis ranks 5th with FDR = 3.98e-08. The converging evidence across ORA, KEGG PSEA, and m/z-network paradigms identifies coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism as the primary biological story. The driver metabolites span both the biogenic-amine branch (L-tryptophan as substrate, serotonin and melatonin as products via tryptophan 5-monooxygenase, EC 1.13.11.11) and the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid as a downstream intermediate).
